messages:
alex: seeing a weird spike in preempt evictions in us-west1, lots of GPU pods being bounced across AZs. latency up for a few jobs :rotating_light:
maria: confirmed — noticed sudden AZ skew in the binpack graph around 14:02 UTC, autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough
sam: rolling change to the scheduler configmap last night (nodeTopologyWeight bump) — could be influencing scoring, will check the diff
jen: ugh yeah i flipped EvenPodsSpread weight from 10 -> 80 in the canary to reduce cross-node spreads for some job classes, thought it was safe
priya: those GPU training pods have topologySpreadConstraint + nodeAffinity for gpu-type=rtx. If scheduler favors AZ-local nodes now, they end up concentrating and evicting spot-backed pods elsewhere
alex: grabbing an example pod + events:
```
kubectl -n training get pod gpu-train-7f8c -o wide
kubectl -n training describe pod gpu-train-7f8c | sed -n '1,120p'
kubectl -n kube-system get events --field-selector type=Warning | grep -i preempt
```
priya: logs show "Preempting pods to make room for higher priority pod": scheduler scored nodes in us-west1-c much higher than a/b
sam: checking scheduler logs now: looks like the scoring plugin that weights topology is multiplying by node.label.zoneScore which got populated by a tweak in the node-prober yesterday
maria: we should mitigate fast — customers are seeing batch failures and cost is spiking because pods reschedule and reattach GPUs
infra-bot: ALERT: #infra-gpu-util peaked at 93% in us-west1-c. Pager duty: oncall@redwood.inc
jen: ok rollback plan: revert the weight bump in configmap to previous values and restart scheduler on canary first
alex: pragmatic quick fix: cordon the most saturated nodes in us-west1-c that are causing preemptions and scale up dedicated pool in us-west1-a/b to spread load. Doing now:
```
kubectl -n kube-system cordon gpu-node-uw1c-12
gcloud compute instances group managed resize gpu-pool-uw1a --size=6
```
priya: also patch problematic deployments to add `topologySpreadConstraints` with `whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule` where possible, reduces churn
sam: i'll prepare the configmap revert PR and run it through canary, but need someone to monitor autoscaler + spot reclaim while we flip
maria: i'll babysit metrics and open a dashboard link here: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/gpu/az-skew?orgId=1
jen: long term we should gate topology-weight rollouts behind a canary that simulates binpack shapes + an integration test that exercises spot reclaim + PDBs
alex: agreed. also add cost alert for repeated preempt-reschedule cycles (runs >3 restarts within 10m) — that's burning GPUs and $$
sam: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler-config/commit/abc123 — reverting weight to 10, will apply to canary scheduler at 1769005000ish
priya: after revert, i'll run a synthetic placement test to ensure pods spread back out before we uncordon nodes
jen: nice. once stable we'll add a small playbook in eng-platform runbook lib
maria: current status: cordoned 2 nodes, autoscaler requested +2 in uw1a, eviction rate dropping :thumbsup:
alex: thanks all. i'll follow up with a short incident note and we can decide whether to post a postmortem if this recurs
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 (investigating scheduler topology weight rollout). Pager duty updated.
